title: Поиски загранпаспорта  (Searching for the Travel Passport)

segments.t: In the office, Vika and Kristina pressure Chef Barinov to accept the masterclass because the restaurant desperately needs the publicity during Barani's two-day trip to Russia. Back at the apartment, Max panics when he realizes he cannot find his travel passport before the flight to Cyprus.
Это всех касается.
Между прочим.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
Так чувствовал.
Пардон, не смотрю.
А чего вы не на работе?
Мы во вторую смену.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
А если я паспорт не найду.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Это всех касается.
'This applies to everyone.' Holding firm smoothly with Vika, the "-sya" ending on "kasayetsya" ("concerns, applies to") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
Между прочим.
'By the way.' Vika jumps in warmly in their talk, making her position completely clear.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
'And here is why, Viktor Petrovich.' Following up firmly beside Barinov, Kostya links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
'He is in Russia for only two days.' Cutting in calmly in this beat, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
'We need the publicity, Vitya.' Vika steps in steadily beside Barinov, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
'That is why I did not want to go there.' Kostya steps in plainly before Vika and reaches for the Russian word "idti" ("to go") right at the heart of the line.
Так чувствовал.
'I had a feeling about it.' Pressing on quietly with Kostya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Пардон, не смотрю.
'Pardon me, I am not looking.' Vika steps in boldly toward Barinov, to clear the air between them once and for all.
А чего вы не на работе?
'Why are you guys not at work?' Mentioning the work on the spot, Kostya brings in "rabote" ("work", from "rabota") as the key Russian word here.
Мы во вторую смену.
'We are on the second shift.' Pointing out how second things are in this beat, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
'Listen, Kostyan, have you seen my travel passport?' Vika questions point-blank whether Kostya really thought this through.
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
'Kristina just offered Sasha two vouchers to Cyprus.' Pointing to the vouchers on the spot, Kostya brings in "predlozhila" ("to offer, to suggest", from "predlozhit") as the key Russian word here.
А если я паспорт не найду.
'And what if I do not find the passport.' Highlighting the passport in the exchange, Barinov brings in "pasport" ("passport") to make the meaning unmistakable.
Это всех касается.
Между прочим.
А вот зачем, Виктор Петрович.
Он всего лишь два дня в России.
Нам нужен пиар, Витя.
Вот почему я так не хотел туда идти.
Так чувствовал.
Пардон, не смотрю.
А чего вы не на работе?
Мы во вторую смену.
Слушай, Костян, ты не видел мой загранпаспорт?
Просто Кристина предложила Сашу две путевки на Кипр.
А если я паспорт не найду.

That wraps up this scene as vika and Kristina insist that Claude Monet needs the PR from Barani's two-day visit to Russia, while Max frantically searches his apartment with Kostya for his foreign passport. See you next time!
До свидания!
